_comment: RViT+ V5 configuration. CONV-FREE, RL-ONLY, MEMORY-AS-TOKENS variant. Sibling of RViT_plus_v4/ — IDENTICAL except the encoder. The image is patchified (reshape + MLP, no Conv2d) into a token grid and consumed by a 2-layer MEMORY-AS-TOKENS transformer (Palladio FBT_MemTok): each layer self-attends over [patch tokens ++ H1 ++ H2] = 3*n_tokens tokens (NO FiLM; all memory sent in as feedback tokens, tagged by a learned source embedding {patch,H1,H2}), and a per-layer shared LSTMCell updates that layer's memory from the patch-token outputs. The two recurrent states H1,H2 are read by 2-layer Transformer actor/critic decoders with a prepended CLS token (unchanged from v4). NO decoder/recon, NO VAE, NO predictive-coding/JEPA. Training = PAC actor loss (MPO E-step + BC) + distributional QR-DQN critic + prioritized episode replay, identical to v3/v4. Priority for any setting: CLI arg > this config > script-hardcoded default.

run._note_init_mode: fresh = random init (checkpoint_path ignored); warm_start = partial load (skip name/shape mismatches silently); resume = strict load (fail on any mismatch). v5 starts fresh — its encoder tensors don't match v4's FiLM encoder, so there is nothing to warm-start from.
run._note_checkpoint_location: checkpoint_dir points OUTSIDE the repo (~/rvit_plus_checkpoints/v5) on purpose: the AttentionManuscript repo is a Google Drive sync root (.tmp.driveupload/.tmp.drivedownload at its top level) and Drive was observed rewriting checkpoints mid-session, which can corrupt a run. Keep live checkpoints in a non-synced home dir; copy a final one back into the repo manually if you want it backed up (but NOT during a live run).

environment._comment: ChangeDetectionEnv parameters — matched to the v3/HRA defaults for apples-to-apples comparison.

model._comment: Conv-free patch + 2-layer memory-as-tokens transformer + 2-layer Transformer actor/critic decoders.
model._note_patch: patch_size must divide the 50x50 image: {1,2,5,10,25,50}. patch_size=5 → 10x10 grid = 100 tokens (each 25x25 Gabor quadrant = a 5x5 patch block). 50 is not divisible by 16, so a literal 16x16 grid does not tile the image; 5 is the cleanest fine-grid divisor.
model._note_patch_hidden: The raw flattened patch is small (patch_dim = C*p*p = 3*5*5 = 75, of which only ~25 are unique because the env replicates each Gabor across the 3 RGB channels). A per-patch MLP (Linear→GELU→Linear→LayerNorm) of hidden width patch_hidden expands it up to d_model before the recurrent/transformer nets — the conv-free analog of v3's normed V1 stem. Default 128 = d_model.
model._note_d_model: d_model MUST equal d_mem in v5: the memory rows are concatenated into the same d_model token stream as the patch tokens (memory-as-tokens), so they must share the width.
model._note_enc_layers: Number of memory-as-tokens layers = number of recurrent memory states. Each layer self-attends over [patch tokens ++ ALL memories] = (1+enc_layers)*n_tokens tokens; with enc_layers=2 that is 3*n_tokens (the spec's 'N_tokens x 3'). The decoders read all enc_layers memory states.
model._note_n_FR: Inner iterations per frame. 1 = one pass per frame. >1 re-reads the same patch tokens while the token-memories settle.
model._note_head: Each decoder reads its CLS vector through an MLP readout head of head_layers Linear layers (minimum 2) with hidden width head_hidden. head_layers=2 → Linear(d_mem→head_hidden)→GELU→Dropout→Linear(head_hidden→out). The final Linear is small-init'd so initial logits/values are ~0; the actor's init_action_bias sits on its bias. head_hidden defaults to d_mem.
model._note_rl_heads: Actor + distributional critic, each a 2-layer Transformer reading [CLS] + concat(H1,H2). init_action_bias = [wait_bias, press_bias]; [0.0, -1.5] gives initial P(press)≈0.18 so episodes run long enough to generate a learning signal before the policy moves.

ppo._comment: PAC actor loss (MPO E-step + BC) + distributional QR-DQN critic + prioritized episode replay. RL ONLY — no recon, no PC, no pretrain.
ppo._note_pac_actor: PAC (Springenberg, Abdolmaleki et al., DeepMind 2024) REPLACES PPO's clipped surrogate. Discrete MPO E-step is closed-form: q(a|s) = softmax_a[ log π_old(a|s) + Q̄(s,a)/η ]; M-step + BC blend gives L_actor = (1−α)·[−Σ_a q(a|s)·log π_θ(a|s)] + α·[−log π_θ(a_t|s)]. η = mpo_temperature, α = bc_alpha.
ppo._note_target_network: PAC target network θ' (Springenberg et al. 2024, §3.2): the critic's distributional TD target AND the MPO E-step reference policy π_θ' BOTH come from a periodically hard-copied, time-lagged copy of θ. target_update_period = hard-copy θ→θ' every N optimizer steps; 0 disables (online bootstrap). The main stabilizer for the bootstrapped actor-critic; was missing in the original implementation.
ppo._note_burn_in: Burn-in / wait-pretrain (v3's recon_pretrain_iters, restored 2026-06-06). For the first burn_in_iters iterations the agent is FORCED to wait (action=0) so episodes run full-length, and only the critic is trained with the actor FROZEN at init — warming up the value function and recurrent representation on clean full trajectories before the policy acts. v5 has no decoder/recon (and no contrastive), so the critic/representation warm up alone. 0 disables.
ppo._note_per: Prioritized episode replay (Schaul et al. 2016, episode-level). Fresh on-policy episodes are augmented with per_n_replay replay episodes sampled ∝ priority^per_alpha (priority = mean per-step quantile-Huber error, clipped at per_priority_clip×median). IS weights (1/(N·p))^β with β annealed per_beta_start→per_beta_end over the run. per_n_replay=0 disables replay.
